subject.title: Subagent lifecycle observability + async supervision controls

question: Which core contract should own durable subagent lifecycle receipts and audited cancel/steer/resume supervision: the task ledger, the audit ledger, or a dedicated subagent lifecycle API?
rationale: The remaining work defines persistent state, Gateway protocol, operator permissions, redaction, retention, artifact references, and mutation audit semantics, so automation should not choose the public security boundary.

options.title: Extend existing ledgers
options.body: Use task summaries for run state, audit events for supervision receipts, and artifact RPCs for pointers so operators get one coherent model without a parallel store.

options.title: Create a lifecycle API
options.body: Add a dedicated SQLite-backed subagent lifecycle ledger and Gateway API if task and audit records cannot express ordered receipts and action semantics cleanly.

options.title: Defer to narrower slices
options.body: Keep UI timeline or channel-liveness issues moving while postponing the durable supervision contract until maintainers are ready to define the boundary.

recommendation.title: Extend existing ledgers
recommendation.body: Use task summaries for run state, audit events for supervision receipts, and artifact RPCs for pointers so operators get one coherent model without a parallel store.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across subagent control, registry lifecycle, and the product/security boundary this decision would reshape.
